fresh.text: The original run cannot be singled out from the surviving evidence. Use {path} as the file in both commands of the static JSONL example. Write a new run with a fresh unique marker, exit, then reopen that file in a second process. Match exactly one row and read its decision_id. The new ID identifies only the new run.

memory_lost.text: The in-memory decision ended with the process. Its printed copy would be in retained stdout. With no retained output, the original remains unknown. For a new test, use the complete JSONL example in the static guide. Give the new run a unique marker, exit, then open the file in another process and match that marker. This verifies only the new run.

future.text: For a new test, use the complete JSONL example in the static guide. Give the new run a unique marker, exit, then open the file in another process and match that marker. This verifies only the new run.

jsonl.text: Open {path} in a second process, resolving a relative path from the original working directory. Search all rows for {correlation}. One matching decision verifies that record reached the file. Older rows, multiple matches, or unreadable lines leave the original unverified. If only older or unrelated rows are present, there is no match for this run in the inspected file.

memory.text: Inspect {stdout} for the Python quickstart’s printed decision and match the original ID or unique marker. Its in-memory list ended when the process exited.

console.text: Inspect {stderr} for the console exporter’s decision JSON. Match the original ID or unique marker to verify a retained copy.

reply.text: Read {stdout} from the application for the printed reply text. The decision metadata is a separate artifact.

node_console.text: Inspect {stderr} for decision_type and token_usage.total_tokens in the JSON decision. The demo prints its reply to stdout. Default Node capture omits prompt and reply content from inputs and outputs.

node_file.text: Open {path} from the launch directory and match the original decision ID or unique marker. Inspect decision_type and token_usage.total_tokens in the matching row. The demo prints its application reply to stdout.

hosted.text: Open the workspace and agent that received the submission. Match {correlation} against the hosted run ID in the run details.

receiver.text: Search the HTTP receiver’s received batch contents for {correlation}. A matching entry verifies receipt. A URL, status code, or a different ID leaves receipt unconfirmed. Verify storage separately by querying the downstream store for the same ID.

otlp.text: Search the collector’s received briefcase.decision spans for {correlation}. A matching span proves collector receipt. Query downstream storage for the same correlation to verify persistence. Confirm the OTLP exporter initialized in the original runtime. If Python logged an initialization fallback, inspect its actual exporter and retained stream.

endpoint.text: Search the receiver’s log or received spans for {correlation}. A configured endpoint leaves receipt unknown. Verify storage with a separate downstream query for the same ID.

storage.text: The matching receiver entry verifies receipt of this decision. Downstream storage is unverified until a separate readback matches. Query downstream storage for {correlation} and compare the returned ID or trace correlation.

stored.text: The matching downstream readback verifies storage of that decision at the time of the query. Compare the identifier in the returned row or span with {correlation} and retain the query result as evidence.

ask_path.text: What JSONL path did the original process use? Enter the path from its launch configuration.

ask_id.text: What original decision ID or marker unique to this invocation do you have? Identical ticket text cannot distinguish the runs. If no identifier survives, the original remains unknown.

ask_program.text: Which Python script did the launcher actually execute? Check its command or log for the quickstart that prints its memory record, or the application using an exporter.

ask_subject.text: Which artifact are you trying to find: the application’s reply text, a local SDK decision, or a submitted run in a hosted workspace?

ask_exporter.text: Which exporter did the original process use? Check the launch configuration and any explicit in-code exporter. For a file, give the original path. The current shell alone is a clue.

ask_protocol.text: Did the original process send JSON over HTTP or export OTLP spans? Check its launch configuration.

fallback.text: Use the static guide below to check the original launch command, retained output, or known destination. The original remains unidentified until evidence matches it.

jsonl_stale.text: The observed rows in {path} do not match {correlation}. This file gives no readback for the original run. Resolve the path from the original launch directory and check the original ID or unique marker before attributing a different row.

ask_run.text: Did the original launch create a local SDK decision or submit a hosted dashboard run? Check the launch command or submission receipt.

local.text: Use the local SDK launch command to identify its exporter. Check retained stderr for console export, retained stdout for a printed memory record, or the original JSONL file for {correlation}. A matching decision identifies the local run.

receipt_unknown.text: Receipt of {correlation} is unconfirmed. Inspect receiver-side entries or received spans for the original ID or trace correlation. A successful request, an endpoint, or an unrelated entry cannot verify delivery of this decision. Verify storage separately with a matching downstream readback.

memory_only.text: A memory exporter keeps the decision in that process. Check whether the program explicitly printed or saved the original ID and decision before exit. If it exited without saving a copy, the in-memory record is gone.

disabled.text: The original inherited settings disable this exporter. Check the original application for an explicit alternate exporter or a separately retained copy. A disabled export provides no receiver or storage evidence.

check_launch.text: Inspect the original launch configuration, runtime and explicit exporter or plugin settings. Use the destination they identify to check for the original decision ID. The inherited settings alone cannot establish that a record was emitted.

defaults.correlation: the original ID or unique marker

guide:
Find the original record

Start with the original decision ID or a value unique to that invocation. If several runs reused a ticket, obtain the original ID from a launch log or retained output. The ticket alone cannot identify the original.

Which Python script ran? The Python quickstart uses memory and prints its decision to stdout. After exit, check retained stdout. The console exporter writes decision JSON to stderr. For a redirected stream, inspect the file named by the original launch command.

Which output do you want? The Node demo prints the app reply to stdout. Its console decision on stderr contains decision_type and token_usage.total_tokens. An explicitly selected or inherited JSONL exporter sends that metadata to its file. For a hosted submission, match its run ID in the receiving workspace and agent.

Check the original exporter and working directory. An explicit in-code exporter takes precedence over an inherited default. For JSONL, reopen the file in a separate process and inspect every row for the original ID or unique marker. Zero matches, multiple matches or unreadable lines leave attribution unresolved.

For HTTP, find the original ID in a received batch. For OTLP, find its briefcase.decision span using the original trace correlation. A URL or HTTP status leaves receipt unverified. A matching receiver entry proves receipt. Query downstream storage separately for that same ID.

Verify a new local run with these two Python commands from the same directory. Enter the same JSONL path at both prompts, or press Enter at both to use record-check.jsonl. The writer appends a new decision and prints the synthetic marker. Paste it when the second asks. A unique match proves only the new run.

python -c 'import uuid, briefcase; marker=str(uuid.uuid4()); briefcase.observe(input("JSONL path [record-check.jsonl]: ").strip() or "record-check.jsonl"); briefcase.capture(lambda ticket: "ok")(marker); print(marker)'

python -c 'import json; path=input("JSONL path [record-check.jsonl]: ").strip() or "record-check.jsonl"; marker=input("New marker: ").strip(); rows=[json.loads(line) for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8")]; hits=[r for r in rows if marker and r.get("inputs", {}).get("args") == repr((marker,))]; print("Matches:", len(hits), [r.get("decision_id") for r in hits])'
